name: match
detail: match self { FParse => the declared subset is exactly what the frontend can read, and everything outside it is reported rather than assumed analysed FUndefinedName => the visible binding set is complete: this file, the extern .mbti tables, the builtins -- confidence is low because the conclusion rests on names, not declarations FUnusedLocal => the frame audit saw every read, and no unread region could reach the declaration FUnusedParam => the function contains no unread region, so no read could have been missed FParamChanged => the assignment was observed directly, which an unread region cannot undo FAssignType => both types are known; an unknown type on either side absorbs the error FArgType => the callee's signature is known: declared in this file, or in the extern .mbti tables FOpMismatch => neither operand is unknown, and both types are within the operator table FMethodError => both operands are concrete; an unknown operand absorbs FCondBool => the condition's type is known, and the branch was not constant-folded FUnreachable => the behavioral lens executes the body and joins branches, so a terminator inside a BRANCH does not by itself kill what follows -- but the join is over ONE execution: when a callee's parameter was bound from the caller's argument, a branch decided by that value can still kill the rest of the body (measured; see the family's `excluded`) FStaleNosec => a suppression matches a report on the same start line whose family it names FInfeasibleBranch => facts come only from a guard comparing an IMMUTABLE local binding against a LITERAL, within one function; a rebound, aliased or non-literal operand carries no fact FRedundantGuard => the same fragment: an immutable binding against a literal, with integer comparisons that do not wrap and no reassignment between the two guards}

name: match
detail: match self { FParse => nothing about the skipped construct's meaning: a notice is not a defect, and one notice per construct does not enumerate what is inside it FUndefinedName => names a dependency or a macro could bind; the state-machine frontend reuses this id for an undefined state name FUnusedLocal => reads inside a region the parser cut in half; a write-only binding is still reported FUnusedParam => any read in a function whose text contains an unread region -- the whole function is silenced FParamChanged => the same as UnusedParam: an unread region silences it, even though an observed assignment cannot be un-observed FAssignType => unannotated rebinding, which widens with a join; and field assignment targets, which are unchecked FArgType => calls to a callee with no visible signature -- those are counted unchecked, not reported; and named-call arity FOpMismatch => unknown operand types; the pipe operator and regex-match operands are exempt FMethodError => a call outside the per-file method table; the state-machine frontend reuses this id for a call on a state operation FCondBool => constant-folded conditions and unknown types; the state-machine frontend reuses this id for a non-boolean guard FUnreachable => DEAD CODE in the deck's sense -- executed but irrelevant, a value overwritten before use -- is reported by NO family, this one included; path feasibility, which needs semantics and is undecidable in general, is reported under MSA-013 only when a BOUNDED constraint model can show the domain empty; and THIS FAMILY OVER-REPORTS when a callee's parameter was bound from the caller's argument, so an `if` whose condition came from outside can kill the rest of the body on one input and be reported for all of them (measured 2026-11-07, pinned by pipeline_0524_test); the state-machine frontend reuses this id for a state outside the reachability closure FStaleNosec => whether the suppressed finding was real FInfeasibleBranch => feasibility that needs a call result, an index, an arithmetic identity or an interprocedural fact -- undecidable in general, so a branch this model cannot decide is counted UNDECIDED rather than claimed reachable FRedundantGuard => the same fragment; a test whose operand was mutated after the binding carries no fact, so it is undecided rather than reported}

name: match
detail: match self { FParse => Advice::{ why : The frontend did not read a construct, or a file-kind frontend rejected a shape. On a .mbt this marks the FIRST genuine read failure in the file: every finding at or after that line is withheld, because it would be derived from an already-wrong tree. On .mbti / .mbt.md / .mbtp it is a frontend rule (malformed line, duplicate signature, unresolvable type reference) rather than a parse boundary., how : Fix the FIRST parse error only — it is the boundary, and later ones are frequently its consequences. If the message is 'test declaration is outside the analyzed subset' or 'struct declaration is outside the analyzed subset', it is a declared scope limit of this analyzer, not a defect: there is nothing to fix, and the finding is rendered 'notice:' rather than 'error:' for exactly that reason. If it is 'unknown type ... in interface signature', the .mbti lens has no cross-file awareness and the type may well be declared in a sibling package; treat that finding as unverified rather than acting on it.,} FUnusedLocal => Advice::{ why : A local binding was assigned and never read anywhere in the function. The scan is not flow-sensitive, so a read inside an unreachable or dead branch still counts as a use., how : Remove the binding, or read it. A name that starts with `_` is exempt, matching the compiler: a discard binding (`let _ = f(x)`, a `for k, _ in pairs` binder, or the unused second half of `let (count, _classes) = refine()`) is how MoonBit says 'I mean to drop this', so reporting it would contradict the toolchain. Verified by probe, not assumed — `moon check` stays silent on `_f` / `_classes` while warning on a `plain` control in the same file. This wording reversed the rule in 0.4.13; before that, an underscore-PREFIXED name was reported on the reasoning that 'a name is not a discard pile', which the toolchain does not agree with.,} FUnusedParam => Advice::{ why : A parameter was never read in the function body. Writing THROUGH a parameter counts as a read, so `self.field = v` and `v[0] = x` do not trigger this; only a parameter that is genuinely never touched does., how : Remove the parameter and its argument at every call site, or keep it for signature compatibility and accept the warning. A parameter named exactly `_` is exempt — the same discard idiom as locals; an underscore-PREFIXED name is not exempt. This wording reversed the rule in 0.4.13: a probe settled that `moon check` does NOT warn on an unused `_f`, only on a non-underscore control in the same file, so the prefix is exempt here too.,} FParamChanged => Advice::{ why : A parameter's BINDING was rebound by a bare assignment — `p = expr` or `p += 1` — so from the next read on, `p` names something the caller never passed. Writing THROUGH a parameter is not this: MoonBit structs are references, so `self.field = v`, `v[0] = x` and `pair.0 = x` mutate the object the parameter points at and leave the parameter itself alone, and those do not report., how : If the rebinding is deliberate, accept the finding as advisory. If you meant to reach a field or an element, write that target directly instead of the parameter. If you need the original value after the write, copy it first: `let mut copy = p`, then assign to `copy` — that is also the fix for a genuine rebind, because it makes the change local to the call.,} FAssignType => Advice::{ why : The right-hand side's inferred type is not assignable to the declared annotation. `Unknown` is always assignable, so a finding here means both sides were resolvable and disagreed., how : Correct the annotation, or convert the value. Caveat: optional types (`String?`) and the `None` literal are not modelled by the type lens, so a `None` passed into an optional parameter can be typed as something unrelated and report here; verify against `moon check` before acting.,} FArgType => Advice::{ why : Either an argument's type is not assignable to the declared parameter, or more arguments were passed than the signature declares. The 'too many arguments' form only runs against a REAL parameter list — a function known only through a `.mbti` declaration is typed as an unknown-signature value and is never arity-checked., how : Check the declared parameter type at the call site. If this is an 'expected N, got M' on a cross-package call, confirm the callee's real signature first: this analyzer skips the check precisely because it cannot see the signature, so a report here means it did see one.,} FOpMismatch => Advice::{ why : One of four shapes: `!` applied to a non-boolean; a binary operator applied to operand types it does not accept; a value that is known not to be callable being called; or a list index that is not an integer. A callee whose type is `Unknown` is never reported — an unresolved type is not evidence of anything., how : For an operand error, check both sides against the operator's domain. For 'not callable', the callee's type is known and is not a function — name a function, or call the method on the receiver. For a list index, pass an Int.,} FMethodError => Advice::{ why : The behavioral lens could not find a method matching the operator or function on the abstract values it computed for the operands. It reasons about the concrete values it can fold, so it is the lens that reports most precisely and the one least likely to be the tool's blindness., how : Confirm the receiver type and the method's parameter types at the call site. This family is raised by the behavioral lens on folded constant values, so a finding usually corresponds to a real compile error.,} FCondBool => Advice::{ why : A condition's type is known and is not boolean. As with the operand checks, an `Unknown` condition is never reported., how : Make the condition a boolean expression — compare explicitly, or replace a non-boolean value with a test on it.,} FUndefinedName => Advice::{ why : No visible binding for the name: not declared in this file, not a builtin, and not present in the cross-file symbol table. The wording says which lens saw it — `no visible binding` (structural), `undefined name` (type), `undefined variable` / `undefined function` (behavior). All three consult the same table, so one finding means all three looked., how : Declare it, import it, or — when it lives in another package — index that package's interface with `--extern-iface-dir <dir>` (target `.repos/` after `moon fetch`). TWO known limits, both unfixable from the CLI: a `#doc(hidden)` API appears in no `.mbti` and so cannot be indexed that way, and a top-level cross-package reference written `@pkg.fn(1, 2)` is not folded into a callable name by the parser, so it is reported even when the package is indexed.,} FUnreachable => Advice::{ why : UNREACHABLE CODE: no execution reaches this statement, because the flow arriving at it has already left the block. The behavioral lens decides this while executing the body, and it joins branches -- so a `return` inside an `if` does NOT by itself make what follows dead, and code after an `if` whose EVERY branch terminates does.
